seo.metaTitle: Rotate PNG - Free Image Rotator, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Rotate a PNG by 90, 180 or 270 degrees in your browser. Lossless, no quality loss, no upload of your file. Free, no signup, no limits.
seo.longDescription: Rotate PNG turns the picture by 90, 180 or 270 degrees. Because the angle is a multiple of 90, the pixels are only moved to new positions: nothing is resampled, nothing is interpolated and no quality is lost — which is not true of arbitrary-angle rotation. The canvas follows the new orientation, so a portrait shot becomes landscape and nothing gets cropped. It all happens in your browser, so screenshots, scans and private photos can be turned without leaving your device.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Only right angles, on purpose: pixels move without resampling — bit-for-bit sharp.
Width and height swap at 90 and 270 degrees; no part of the picture is cropped.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Pick the angle: 90 degrees clockwise turns it a quarter turn, 180 flips it upside down, 270 turns it the other way.
Check the preview: the dimensions under the tile swap for portrait and landscape.
Download the result from the Download button in any of the four formats.

faq.q: Can I rotate by an angle that is not 90, 180 or 270?
faq.a: Not here, on purpose. An arbitrary angle resamples every pixel, which softens edges and can cut the corners off. The three right-angle options move pixels only, so the result is bit-for-bit as sharp as the source.

faq.q: Does rotating lose quality or blur the image?
faq.a: No. The rotation is a pure remapping of pixel positions, exactly as rotating a physical photo on the scanner glass would. There is no interpolation step and no re-compression inside the tool.

faq.q: Will part of my image be cut off?
faq.a: No. The canvas is resized to the new orientation, so the full picture survives the turn. Width and height simply swap when you rotate by 90 or 270 degrees.

faq.q: How do I flip the image instead of rotating it?
faq.a: Use the flip tool on this site: it mirrors the picture horizontally or vertically, which is what you want for a mirrored selfie or a scanned page. Rotation turns the picture, flipping turns it inside out.
